boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-cost outings across Chester County’s seven regional parks and three regional trails, all officially confirmed free to visit.

cards.title: Follow the Wetland Interpretive Trail
cards.subtitle: An accessible nature walk near Phoenixville
cards.notes: Walk the 0.8-mile interpretive loop together and pause at the wetlands to look for amphibians, waterfowl and seasonal changes.
cards.short_summary: A short, ADA-accessible loop turns a reclaimed industrial landscape into an easy group nature outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County identifies Black Rock Sanctuary as a county park and states that all county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Public county park; visit between 8:00 a.m. and the posted seasonal closing time. No admission or purchase is required.

cards.title: Pack a Picnic for Exton Park
cards.subtitle: Trails and open space in Exton
cards.notes: Bring food from home, claim an unreserved picnic spot and pair lunch with a walk through the park’s connected trail network.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own picnic makes this large shared county-and-township park a flexible, purchase-free meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County lists Exton County Park among its seven county parks and confirms that all county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Public county park; open from 8:00 a.m. to the applicable seasonal closing time. Paid reservations are unnecessary for a casual visit.

cards.title: Take a Group Hike at Hibernia
cards.subtitle: Woodland trails around a historic county park
cards.notes: Choose a park trail that fits the group’s pace, carry water and leave time to view the grounds around historic Hibernia Mansion.
cards.short_summary: Woodland paths and historic scenery provide a full afternoon outing without an entrance charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County names Hibernia County Park as a county park and explicitly says all county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Public county park; arrive after 8:00 a.m. and leave by the posted seasonal closing time. Ordinary park access is free.

cards.title: Meet for an Outdoor Lunch
cards.subtitle: A bring-your-own gathering in southern Chester County
cards.notes: Pack lunch and a blanket, use an available picnic area and add a walk among the park’s distinctive serpentine-barren landscape.
cards.short_summary: Picnic space and unusual natural terrain create an unhurried group outing with nothing to buy.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County identifies Nottingham County Park as one of its county parks and states that every county park and trail is free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Public county park; standard access runs from 8:00 a.m. to the seasonal closing time. Bring your own supplies to keep the outing free.

cards.title: Visit the Farm Animals
cards.subtitle: A demonstration-farm meetup in Glenmoore
cards.notes: Stop by the barn complex to see the farm animals, then follow a marked trail through the fields, woodland edges and historic landscape.
cards.short_summary: Animals, agricultural history and walking trails combine in a varied no-admission outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County lists Springton Manor Farm as a county park and confirms that all its county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 8:00 a.m. to the seasonal closing time; the barn and museum are normally open 10:00 a.m.–2:30 p.m. Admission is free.

cards.title: Bring a Ball for Lawn Games
cards.subtitle: An active afternoon beside French Creek
cards.notes: Pack a ball or flying disc, use an open recreation area and cool down afterward with a walk along the park’s creekside trails.
cards.short_summary: Open recreation space and wooded paths let a group mix casual games with a nature walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County identifies Warwick County Park as a county park and says all county parks and trails are available free of charge.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Public county park; use the grounds from 8:00 a.m. until the posted seasonal closing time. No admission or purchase is required.

cards.title: Go Birding in Wolf’s Hollow
cards.subtitle: A rustic woodland outing near Atglen
cards.notes: Bring binoculars if you have them, select a trail suited to the group and scan the mature woodland for tanagers, orioles and thrashers.
cards.short_summary: Nearly ten miles of rustic trails offer a quiet, equipment-optional birding meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County lists Wolf's Hollow County Park among its county parks and states that all county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8:00 a.m. to sunset except Christmas Day. Facilities are limited, so carry water and pack out trash; access is free.

cards.title: Walk the Chester Valley Trail
cards.subtitle: A paved regional-trail meetup near Exton
cards.notes: Pick a public trailhead, agree on a turnaround point and use the smooth multi-use path for an easy out-and-back walk with friends.
cards.short_summary: A paved regional route makes distance and pace easy to adjust for a casual social walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County identifies the Chester Valley Trail as a county regional trail and confirms that all county parks and trails are free.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open one-half hour before sunrise until one-half hour after sunset. Walking requires no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Plan a River-Trail Bike Ride
cards.subtitle: A choose-your-distance ride on a county trail
cards.notes: Meet at a public trailhead with your own bikes, choose a comfortable turnaround landmark and keep right while sharing the multi-use path.
cards.short_summary: The county-managed trail segment supports a flexible ride using equipment you already own.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County names the Schuylkill River Trail as a regional county trail and states that all county parks and trails are free to visit.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset. Trail use is free; this activity assumes participants bring their own bicycles.

cards.title: Take a Creekside Stroll
cards.subtitle: A relaxed multi-use trail outing near Downingtown
cards.notes: Start from a public trailhead, walk beside East Branch Brandywine Creek and choose a turnaround time that leaves daylight for the return.
cards.short_summary: A creekside route provides a straightforward, conversation-friendly walk with no required spending.
cards.evidence_claim: Chester County identifies the Struble Trail as a county regional trail and explicitly confirms that all county parks and trails are free.
cards.source_title: Chester County Parks + Preservation Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Open one-half hour before sunrise until one-half hour after sunset. Public trail access requires no fee or purchase.
